Cross slip.subject: Computer & IT
Cross slip.question: Therefore, a screw dislocation can glide or slip along any plane that contains its _____ vector
Cross slip.fact: Since the Burgers vector of a perfect screw dislocation is parallel to the dislocation line, it has an infinite number of possible slip planes (planes containing the dislocation line and the Burgers vector), unlike an edge or mixed dislocation, which has a unique slip plane. Discrete-time Fourier transform.subject: Computer & IT
Discrete-time Fourier transform.question: Under certain theoretical conditions, described by the sampling theorem, the original continuous function can be recovered perfectly from the _____ and thus from the original discrete samples
Discrete-time Fourier transform.fact: In simpler terms, when you take the DTFT of regularly-spaced samples of a continuous signal, you get repeating (and possibly overlapping) copies of the signal's frequency spectrum, spaced at intervals corresponding to the sampling frequency. Under certain theoretical conditions, described by the sampling theorem, the original continuous function can be recovered perfectly from the DTFT and thus from the original discrete samples.

Discrete-time Fourier transform.subject: Computer & IT

Discrete-time Fourier transform.fact: Under certain theoretical conditions, described by the sampling theorem, the original continuous function can be recovered perfectly from the DTFT and thus from the original discrete samples. The DTFT itself is a continuous function of frequency, but discrete samples of it can be readily calculated via the discrete Fourier transform (DFT) (see § Sampling the DTFT), which is by far the most common method of modern Fourier analysis.

Dominating set.fact: In graph theory, a dominating set for a graph G is a subset D of its vertices, such that any vertex of G is in D, or has a neighbor in D. The dominating set problem concerns testing whether γ(G) ≤ K for a given graph G and input K; it is a classical NP-complete decision problem in computational complexity theory.
